title_de: 53-Man Roster Prediction Pre Training Camp: Wer schafft es in den finalen Roster?
teaser_de: Kurz vor dem Training Camp 2025 ein Tipp für den 53er-Kader der 49ers: Wer setzt sich durch, wer muss zittern?
title_en: 53-man roster prediction before training camp 2025: who makes the final cut?
teaser_en: Right before the 2025 training camp, a pick for the 49ers’ 53-man roster: who makes it and who is on the bubble?
body_en:
Finally, it's that time again: training camp is just around the corner. After a (too long) offseason, the team returns to the practice field for the first time on Wednesday, July 23. Time for a first 53-man roster prediction! The competition for starting jobs and roster spots is bigger than it has been in a long time. A great chance for some young players to push their way forward and make a case for themselves.

There were injury updates on Friday: Ricky Pearsall, Brandon Aiyuk, Andre Dillard, Yetur Gross-Matos, Malik Mustapha and Curtis Robinson are currently on the PUP list. Ben Bartch, Kurtis Rourke and George Odum were placed on the NFI list. Here are the most important terms explained once more:

**PUP list (physically unable to perform list):** The player can be activated at any time. If the player is still on the PUP list after cut day, he automatically misses four games. After that, he can be activated at any time.

**NFI list (non-football injury list):** The rules are exactly the same as for the PUP list. The only difference: players land on the NFI list when their injury happened away from the facility or when they are still injured from their college days.

**Injured reserve (IR):** If a player is placed on IR at this point, he is automatically out for the season and can no longer be activated.

**Waivers/waiver wire:** All players without four accrued seasons are "waived," not released. That means every team has the chance to "claim" (sign) the player before he hits the open market. All players without four accrued seasons must first clear waivers before they can be signed to the practice squad.

### Here is my current 53-man roster prediction:

### Offense

### Quarterback (2)

Last year: Brock Purdy, Brandon Allen, Josh Dobbs (3)

Prediction: Brock Purdy, Mac Jones (2)

Practice squad: Tanner Mordecai

NFI: Kurtis Rourke

Over the past few years, the 49ers have pretty much always had three quarterbacks on the final 53-man roster. This year, however, they have a very clear backup in Mac Jones, and because of the large draft class (11 picks) there aren't as many roster spots available. In addition, we've seen little of Tanner Mordecai in the NFL, which is why I expect him to clear waivers (like last year) and then land on the practice squad.

After tearing his ACL in college, Kurtis Rourke will probably start the season on the NFI list.

### Running back (5)

Last year: Christian McCaffrey, Kyle Juszczyk, Isaac Guerendo, Jordan Mason, Patrick Taylor (5)

Prediction: Christian McCaffrey, Kyle Juszczyk, Isaac Guerendo, Jordan James, Corey Kiner (5)

Practice squad: Patrick Taylor

If CMC, Kyle Juszczyk and Isaac Guerendo are healthy, their roster spots are safe. The same goes for Jordan James as a fifth-round draft pick.

The last spot in the running back room will probably come down to Patrick Taylor and undrafted rookie Corey Kiner. Like the other backs, Kiner has the potential to be a factor in both the run game and the passing game. I can very well imagine him making some plays in the preseason. Taylor has the advantage of being a veteran who already knows the system after a year. But in his appearances last year, he didn't really convince, which is why I'm going with Corey Kiner here.

### Tight end (3)

Last year: George Kittle, Jake Tonges (2); Eric Saubert was released and then immediately brought back

Prediction: George Kittle, Luke Farrell, Jake Tonges (3)

George Kittle and Luke Farrell are clear no-brainers.

Ross Dwelley, Jake Tonges, Brayden Willis and Mason Pline are battling for the third or maybe even fourth spot.

In my prediction, I went with Jake Tonges. He was on the roster all of last year, even though he got little playing time. I therefore assume the team sees a lot of potential in him. In the preseason and in camp last year, he stood out positively again and again.

Dwelley, Willis and Pline are all candidates for the practice squad. Maybe one of the three will make the final roster as well. The easiest way would be with good reps on special teams in the preseason.

### Wide receiver (5)

Last year: Deebo Samuel, Brandon Aiyuk, Jauan Jennings, Ricky Pearsall, Jacob Cowing, Chris Conley, Ronnie Bell (7)

Prediction: Jauan Jennings, Ricky Pearsall, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Junior Bergen (5)

PUP: Brandon Aiyuk

SUS: Demarcus Robinson

As things stand, you can assume that Brandon Aiyuk will start the season on the PUP list and will therefore automatically miss four games. Demarcus Robinson is expected to receive a three-game suspension, since he was arrested for drunk driving in November. The NFL will probably still hand down a suspension here. Jauan Jennings, Ricky Pearsall and Jordan Watkins are safe on the roster. Jacob Cowing should have his place locked up as well.

Junior Bergen, Isaiah Neyor, Russell Gage, Isaiah Hodgins and Terique Owens are fighting for the remaining spots. Because of the new kickoff rule (touchback: drive starts at the 35), I expect the team to keep Junior Bergen as a return specialist.

Then the question is: will the 49ers bet on upside (Isaiah Neyor) or on a veteran like Isaiah Hodgins or Russell Gage? Or will it be Terique Owens, who supposedly caught the eye in practice a few times last season? Or will there be only five wide receivers on the final roster after all? Looking at the roster as a whole, I went with five wide receivers here.

### Offensive tackle (4)

Last year: Trent Williams, Colton McKivitz, Jaylon Moore (3)

Prediction: Trent Williams, Colton McKivitz, Andre Dillard, Spencer Burford (4)

Trent Williams and Colton McKivitz are the starters. Looking at his contract ($315,000 guaranteed), Andre Dillard should also have his spot as a backup locked up.

Burford was the swing tackle for several games last year. He will make the roster and at the same time compete for the starting LG spot.

Austen Pleasants would also be a candidate for one of the backup tackle spots.

### Interior offensive line (5)

Last year: Jake Brendel, Aaron Banks, Dominick Puni, Spencer Burford, Nick Zakelj, Jon Feliciano (6)

Prediction: Jake Brendel, Dominick Puni, Ben Bartch, Matt Hennessy, Connor Colby (5)

Practice squad: Nick Zakelj, Drake Nugent, Drew Moss

Jake Brendel will start at center (whether we like it or not). Dominick Puni is the starting RG.

The LG spot is wide open. Ben Bartch is currently in the "driver's seat" and has gotten all the first-team reps in the offseason program so far. At the moment, however, he is on the NFI list. Unfortunately, there is no information on how serious his injury is. Matt Hennessy, Nick Zakelj and Connor Colby will battle for the remaining places over the next two months.

Matt Hennessy has already started NFL games at LG and at center for the Falcons. In recent years, the 49ers have always had a backup with similar positional flexibility (Feliciano/Brunskill). Maybe Hennessy can even push Jake Brendel out of the starting job.

As a draft pick, Connor Colby should have the best chance at a roster spot. A few weeks ago, he also already received high praise from offensive line coach Chris Foerster. He has the right skill set for this offense and could start, especially in the long run.

Nick Zakelj got real playing time in the regular season for the first time last year. He didn't really convince, so I think he will land on the practice squad along with Drake Nugent.

Drew Moss is a dark-horse candidate for a roster spot. He is definitely someone to keep an eye on.

### Defense

### Defensive tackle (5)

Last year: Javon Hargrave, Maliek Collins, Kevin Givens, Jordan Elliott (4)

Prediction: Kevin Givens, Alfred Collins, CJ West, Jordan Elliott, Evan Anderson (5)

Kevin Givens has by far the most experience with the 49ers, which is why I think the team will continue to rely on him. Jordan Elliott hardly convinced last year, but in this young defensive tackle room his experience could be an advantage. Collins and West have their spots locked up as second- and fourth-round picks respectively.

Evan Anderson already started several games last year as an undrafted free agent. His early flashes were impressive, but he faded badly toward the end. With another offseason and more NFL experience, you could expect Anderson to take the next step.

The odd man out in this scenario would be Kalia Davis. In my view, he simply hasn't shown enough over the past three years. In last year's preseason he made a lot of good plays but then got hurt and couldn't build on those performances in the regular season.

### Defensive end (5)

Last year: Nick Bosa, Leonard Floyd, Yetur Gross-Matos, Robert Beal, Sam Okuayinonu (5)

Prediction: Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Bryce Huff, Sam Okuayinonu, Yetur Gross-Matos (5)

Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams and Bryce Huff have their spots locked up. Under normal circumstances, so does Sam O, who showed his potential several times last year.

A surprise cut candidate could be Yetur Gross-Matos. However, his versatility allows him to help the team in many different roles on the defensive line. Robert Saleh also pretty much always relies on a deep D-line rotation. That's why I think they will keep him.

Robert Beal has shown too little in his first three years. If he performs similarly in training camp, he will probably be waived. The 49ers would then certainly be interested in bringing him back to the practice squad, though.

### Linebacker (6)

Last year: Fred Warner, De'Vondre Campbell, Dee Winters, Tatum Bethune, Demetrius Flannigan-Fowles, Curtis Robinson (6)

Prediction: Fred Warner, Dee Winters, Nick Martin, Tatum Bethune, Luke Gifford, Chazz Surratt (6)

Practice squad: Jalen Graham, Curtis Robinson

Fred Warner, Dee Winters and Nick Martin are the starters.

Luke Gifford and Chazz Surratt are above all core special teamers and therefore have very good chances at a roster spot.

Tatum Bethune showed a lot of promising signs last year (both in the preseason and in the regular season when he got on the field), which is why I expect him to make the roster.

Curtis Robinson would also be a candidate for a roster spot. With him, the question is how healthy he is after his torn ACL (last August). If he performs similarly to last preseason, the 49ers will have to make a tough decision here.

### Cornerback (6)

Last year: Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Charvarius Ward, Isaac Yiadom, Ambry Thomas (5)

Prediction: Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Upton Stout, Tre Brown, Darrell Luter Jr., Siran Neal (6)

Lenoir and Green are probably the starting outside cornerbacks. Tre Brown and rookie Upton Stout are battling for the starting nickel back spot.

Siran Neal received a two-year, $4,000,000 contract in the offseason, of which $2,255,000 is even guaranteed. That locks up his roster spot, and he will mainly take over George Odum's role on special teams.

The 49ers think very highly of Darrell Luter Jr., even though we have seen little of him so far. I think he will survive the final roster cut.

### Safety (4)

Last year: Ji'Ayir Brown, George Odum, Malik Mustapha, Talanoa Hufanga (4)

Prediction: Ji'Ayir Brown, Jason Pinnock, Marques Sigle, Richie Grant (4)

PUP: Malik Mustapha

Malik Mustapha will probably start the season on PUP and, like Brandon Aiyuk, will therefore miss at least four games.

The safety position is more contested than any other on the team. Both starting spots are still wide open. The best chances probably belong to Ji'Ayir Brown, who is entering his third year with the 49ers. Next to him, former New York Giant Jason Pinnock could start. But Richie Grant and Marques Sigle also have a realistic chance at playing time. As already mentioned, anything can happen.

### Special teams (3)

Last year: Jake Moody, Mitch Wishnowsky, Taybor Pepper (3)

Prediction: Jake Moody, Thomas Morstead, Jon Weeks (3)

Thomas Morstead is the starting punter, Jon Weeks the long snapper.

But who will win the kicking competition? Jake Moody or Greg Joseph?

I'm actually betting on Jake Moody. I think the 49ers will keep sticking with him. If Moody has problems again, they still have the option of signing Greg Joseph (or another kicker). If they release Moody, that chapter is probably closed. I don't think the 49ers are ready for that (yet).
